name: Discord

scheme.value: Ed25519 detached signature, hex encoded, verified with the application public key (hex encoded); the docs example uses nacl.sign.detached.verify with hex-decoded signature and public key
scheme.short: Ed25519, hex, checked with the application public key

signed_content.value: The value of X-Signature-Timestamp concatenated directly with the raw request body (timestamp + body, no separator)

header_format.value: X-Signature-Ed25519 carries the signature as a hex string; X-Signature-Timestamp carries the timestamp as a string. One signature, no prefixes or key=value pairs (inferred from the docs code examples, which hex-decode the whole header value)

secret_source.value: The application's public key, found on the application in the Developer Portal
secret_source.quote: Your public key can be found on your application in the Developer Portal

secret_scope.value: Per application (one public key per Discord application)
secret_scope.quote: Your public key can be found on your application in the Developer Portal

raw_body_note.value: The docs JavaScript example uses req.rawBody and notes it is expected to be a string, not raw bytes
raw_body_note.quote: const body = req.rawBody; // rawBody is expected to be a string, not raw bytes

on_invalid_signature.quote: If the signature fails validation, your app should respond with a 401 error code.

node.value: verifyKey(rawBody, signature, timestamp, clientPublicKey), or verifyWebhookEventMiddleware(clientPublicKey), from the discord-interactions npm package (github.com/discord/discord-interactions-js)
node.quote: If you're using an express-like API, you can simplify things by using the `verifyWebhookEventMiddleware`.

python.value: verify_key(raw_body, signature, timestamp, client_public_key) from the discord-interactions PyPI package; its README describes it for signed payloads POSTed to a webhook endpoint and does not mention Webhook Events by name
python.quote: Verify a signed payload POSTed to your webhook endpoint.

method_and_content_type.value: POST (stated for the PING); request content type not stated
method_and_content_type.quote: Discord will send a POST request with a PING payload with a type: 0 to your endpoint.

event_type_location.value: JSON path event.type (string such as APPLICATION_AUTHORIZED); the outer `type` is the webhook type (0 PING, 1 event)
event_type_location.quote: The “Value” column corresponds to the event’s type field value in the event body object.

envelope.value: { version: 1, application_id: <snowflake>, type: 0|1, event: { type: <string>, timestamp: <ISO8601 string>, data: <object> } }; `event` is absent on PING
envelope.quote: Webhook events are wrapped in an outer payload, with an inner event object.

envelope_version.quote: Version scheme for the webhook event. Currently always 1

webhook_type.quote: Type of webhook, either 0 for PING or 1 for webhook events

delivery_id.value: not stated by the provider (no delivery-id header or envelope field is documented; `data.id` on entitlement events is the entitlement ID, not a delivery ID)

handshake.value: When the Webhook Events URL is added, Discord POSTs a PING payload with `type: 0`; the app must acknowledge with HTTP 204 and an empty body (plus a valid Content-Type) and must validate the signature headers, otherwise the URL is not validated
handshake.quote: Your app is expected to acknowledge the request by returning a 204 response with an empty body.
handshake.short: PING (type 0): answer 204, empty body, after verifying

batching.value: One event per request (the envelope carries a single `event` object)
batching.quote: Webhook events are wrapped in an outer payload, with an inner event object.

success_status.quote: your app should respond with a 204 status code with no body within 3 seconds

response_deadline.quote: your app should respond with a 204 status code with no body within 3 seconds

retries.value: If the app does not respond, Discord retries several times with exponential backoff for up to 10 minutes. The number of attempts is not stated.
retries.quote: Discord will retry sending it several times using exponential backoff for up to 10 minutes.
retries.short: Exponential back-off for up to 10 minutes

disabling.value: If the app fails to respond too often, Discord stops sending webhook events and notifies by email. The threshold is not stated. Separately, failing the routine invalid-signature security checks removes the Webhook Events URL and alerts via email and System DM.
disabling.quote: If your app fails to respond too often, Discord will stop sending you webhook events and notify you via email.

security_check_removal.value: Routine automated checks send invalid signatures on purpose; failing them removes the URL
security_check_removal.quote: If you fail the validation, we will remove your Webhook Events URL and alert you via email and System DM.

ordering.value: Not guaranteed in order and not realtime
ordering.quote: events sent over webhooks are not realtime or guaranteed to be in order.

duplicates.value: not stated by the provider (retries imply a repeat can arrive if the 204 is late, but the page does not say so)

common.meaning: App added to a server or user account; data has user, scopes, optional guild and integration_type
common.quote: APPLICATION_AUTHORIZED is sent when the app is added to a server or user account.

common.meaning: A user deauthorized the app; data has the user
common.quote: APPLICATION_DEAUTHORIZED is sent when the app is deauthorized by a user.

common.meaning: A user purchased or was granted one of the app's SKUs; data is an entitlement object
common.quote: ENTITLEMENT_CREATE is sent when an entitlement is created when a user purchases or is otherwise granted one of your app’s SKUs.

common.meaning: An entitlement changed; data is an entitlement object
common.quote: ENTITLEMENT_UPDATE is sent when an entitlement is updated.

common.meaning: An entitlement was deleted; data is an entitlement object
common.quote: ENTITLEMENT_DELETE is sent when an entitlement is deleted.

common.meaning: User added to a Quest; documented but not receivable by apps at present
common.quote: This event cannot be received by apps at this time.

common.meaning: Message created in a Social SDK lobby; data is a lobby message object
common.quote: LOBBY_MESSAGE_CREATE is sent when a message is created in a lobby.

common.meaning: Direct message created during an active Social SDK session
common.quote: Sent when a direct message is created during an active Social SDK session

other_listed_types.quote: Sent when a message is updated in a lobby

where_url_is_entered.value: Developer Portal: the app's Webhooks page (left sidebar), Endpoint field, then toggle Events on and select events, then Save Changes. Via API: Edit Current Application.
where_url_is_entered.quote: Under Endpoint, add a public URL that is set up to receive and acknowledge webhook events.

api_alternative.quote: If you prefer to use the API, you can call Edit Current Application.

gateway_alternative.value: A Webhook Events URL is not needed if the app uses Gateway events
gateway_alternative.quote: If your app is using Gateway events, you don’t need to configure a Webhook Events URL.

test_tools.value: not stated by the provider (the PING sent when the URL is saved is the only documented probe)

gotchas.value: The PING answer here differs from interactions: 204 with an empty body, not 200 with {type: 1}
gotchas.quote: returning a 204 response with an empty body.

gotchas.value: Real events must also be answered 204, no body, within 3 seconds
gotchas.quote: your app should respond with a 204 status code with no body within 3 seconds

gotchas.value: The PING response needs a valid Content-Type
gotchas.quote: You must provide a valid Content-Type when responding to PINGs.

gotchas.value: Webhook events are not realtime and not ordered
gotchas.quote: events sent over webhooks are not realtime or guaranteed to be in order.

gotchas.value: Discord sends deliberately invalid signatures as routine checks and removes the URL if they are accepted
gotchas.quote: including purposefully sending you invalid signatures.

gotchas.value: For Social SDK apps, APPLICATION_DEAUTHORIZED is the only out-of-game signal that a user's link state changed; missing it makes the next token use fail
gotchas.quote: if you miss the webhook, the next token use will fail

delivery_method_and_content_type.value: POST; request content type not stated on these pages (body is the Interaction object JSON)
delivery_method_and_content_type.quote: Discord will send a POST request with a PING payload with a type: 1 to your endpoint.

delivery_event_type_location.value: JSON body field `type` (integer interaction type): PING=1, APPLICATION_COMMAND=2, MESSAGE_COMPONENT=3, APPLICATION_COMMAND_AUTOCOMPLETE=4, MODAL_SUBMIT=5. There is no event-name header.

delivery_delivery_id.value: Body field `id` (snowflake, ID of the interaction). No delivery-id header is documented.

delivery_handshake.value: When the Interactions Endpoint URL is saved, Discord POSTs a PING with `type: 1`; the app must return HTTP 200 with a PONG body `{"type": 1}` and a valid Content-Type, and must also validate the signature headers. If either is incomplete the URL is not validated.
delivery_handshake.quote: returning a 200 response with a PONG payload (which has the same type: 1)

delivery_batching.value: One interaction object per request (the body is a single Interaction object)

responding_success_status.value: HTTP 200 with a JSON Interaction Response object (`type` and optional `data`); for PING, 200 with `{"type": 1}`
responding_success_status.quote: respond with a 200 status code (if everything went well), as well as specifying a type and data

responding_response_deadline.value: 3 seconds for the initial response; if exceeded the interaction token is invalidated
responding_response_deadline.quote: you must send an initial response within 3 seconds of receiving the event. If the 3 second deadline is exceeded, the token will be invalidated.

token_lifetime.value: 15 minutes (interaction token, usable for followup messages and edits)
token_lifetime.quote: Interaction tokens are valid for 15 minutes

responding_disabling.value: Discord runs routine automated security checks against the endpoint, including purposefully sending invalid signatures; failing them removes the Interactions Endpoint URL and alerts via email and System DM. Failure behaviour for ordinary non-responses is not stated.
responding_disabling.quote: purposefully sending you invalid signatures. If you fail the validation, we will remove your interactions URL and alert you via email and System DM.

setup_where_url_is_entered.value: Developer Portal, the application's General Information page, in the Interactive Endpoint URL field
setup_where_url_is_entered.quote: On the General Information page, look for the Interactive Endpoint URL field.

default_transport.value: Without an endpoint URL the app receives interactions over the Gateway; HTTP delivery is opt-in
default_transport.quote: By default your app will receive interactions via a Gateway connection, but you can opt-in to HTTP-based interactions

setup_test_tools.value: not stated by the provider (the PING sent on saving the URL is the only documented probe)

interaction_types.meaning: Handshake sent when the endpoint URL is saved and at other validation times; answer 200 with {type: 1}
interaction_types.quote: returning a 200 response with a PONG payload (which has the same type: 1)

interaction_types.meaning: The response value that acknowledges a PING
Respond to an interaction with a message
interaction_types.quote: CHANNEL_MESSAGE_WITH_SOURCE4Respond to an interaction with a message

interaction_types.meaning: Acknowledge now, edit the response later; the user sees a loading state
interaction_types.quote: ACK an interaction and edit a response later, the user sees a loading state

pitfalls.value: Both the PING answer and the signature validation must be in place before the URL will save; Discord also sends deliberately invalid signatures later and expects 401
pitfalls.quote: If either of these are not complete, your Interactions Endpoint URL will not be validated.

pitfalls.value: The PING response needs a valid Content-Type
pitfalls.quote: You must provide a valid Content-Type when responding to PINGs.

pitfalls.value: The signed message is the timestamp header followed by the body; the docs example treats rawBody as a string, not bytes
pitfalls.quote: rawBody is expected to be a string, not raw bytes

pitfalls.value: Missing the 3 second initial-response deadline invalidates the token
pitfalls.quote: If the 3 second deadline is exceeded, the token will be invalidated.

research_notes: Interactions are not named events; they are typed by the integer `type` field. Response callback types: PONG=1, CHANNEL_MESSAGE_WITH_SOURCE=4, DEFERRED_CHANNEL_MESSAGE_WITH_SOURCE=5 (others exist on the page).

Discord has two HTTP mechanisms with the same signature: the Interactions Endpoint URL (slash commands, buttons; answered with an interaction response) and Webhook Events (app events such as APPLICATION_AUTHORIZED; answered 204). The standard sections above are Webhook Events; the Interactions endpoint section covers the other. The Webhook Events page does not restate the signature algorithm and refers to the Interactions documentation, so the signature facts come from there.
